1. **The advisory (RUSTSEC-2026-0543, chrono).** `cargo deny check advisories` (cargo-deny 0.20.2) at
   2026-11-22T18:34:06Z fetched the advisory database (`~/.cargo/advisory-dbs/advisory-db-3157b0e258782691`, HEAD

   available!`, and `cargo search chrono --limit 1` reads `0.4.45`, the version `Cargo.lock` holds. **No safe upgrade
   exists.** How cargo-deny treats an ignored id once nothing matches it (a no-start probe: `deny.toml` copied to the
   session scratchpad with the chrono id swapped for one no crate of the graph matches, `cargo deny --config
   <copy> check advisories`): the stale ignore reads `warning[advisory-not-detected]: advisory was not encountered`
   (`no crate matched advisory criteria`) — a warning, not an error; the un-ignored chrono advisory read
   `error[unmaintained]` and the check exit 1 (`advisories FAILED`). So once an upgrade leaves chrono out of the
   graph, the standing ignore would surface as that warning, never fail the check by itself.

   `deny.toml`'s reason line already says «re-read at each epoch boundary» (`deny.toml:19`), unchanged.
